Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

  rotated.

59	  `~/.claude` too, and should flag any repo not on `main`/`master`, not just dirty ones.
60	- A pre-merge `git merge-tree` "clean" result is not trustworthy - it reported clean for a merge
61	  that then conflicted on `uv.lock`. Merge into the feature branch first and look.
62	- `projects/**.jsonl` files are live session logs and may change again after a closeout commit when the stop hook writes its final entry.
63	- `scripts/backup-manifest.json` is **not** globally sorted — some `DEV/` entries were appended
64	  after the non-`DEV` block. Insert new entries in place; a full re-sort churns unrelated lines.
65	  `json.dumps(d, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"` round-trips the file byte-identically.

73	  rotated.

75	  prints `Everything up-to-date` to stderr and exits **0**, and the script only records an error

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.


ARGUMENTS: Consolidate global-memory/MEMORY.md (2461/2500 chars, no headroom) to free room without losing facts — move detail to Tier A / STATUS.md pointers.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor

# Claude Stack Doctor

One command surfaces every known silent-failure class in the automation/memory stack. Run it before debugging anything by hand.

## Quick start

```bash
/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File ~/.claude/skills/claude-stack-doctor/scripts/stack-check.ps1   # Mac
pwsh -NoProfile -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\stack-check.ps1                 # Windows
```

The same script runs on both machines and picks its checks by OS (see **Two machines** below). On Windows use `pwsh` 7, not `powershell` 5.1, which reports false `memsearch-run` / `backup-cloud-check` failures.

Exit 0 = all clear. Exit 1 = the VERDICT line lists issue codes. Report the findings to the user, then apply the matching fix below.

## Cross-machine handoff (runs on BOTH machines)

`scripts/handoff-check.ps1` is called at the end of `stack-check.ps1`, and it can also be run on its own:

```
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\skills\claude-stack-doctor\scripts\handoff-check.ps1
```

It answers a question nothing else here asked: did state actually make the trip between the two machines? Every other check verifies a component. This verifies the path.

The failure it exists to catch: `daily-backup` pushes `global-memory` nightly and, until 2026-09-12, nothing on the receiving machine ever pulled it. The Windows laptop was found 4 commits behind with every other signal reading healthy, because the backup section measures `ahead` only — which catches a broken push and is blind to a missing pull.

Issue codes:

- `handoff-memory-stale` — `global-memory` is behind origin. This is the serious one: memory written on the other machine is on GitHub and not here, so this session is running on stale context. Fix with `/startup`, or `git -C ~/.claude/global-memory pull --no-rebase`.
- `handoff-behind:<repo>` — config, skills or notes behind origin. Same fix, lower stakes.
- `handoff-unpushed:<repo>` — this machine is more than 3 commits ahead. The other machine cannot see this work; run `/closeout`.
- `handoff-fetch:<repo>` — offline, or GitHub auth has rotted.
- `handoff-repo-gone:<repo>` — the folder is present but is not a git repo. Something replaced a synced repo with a plain folder and its contents are going nowhere.
- A repo absent from the machine entirely is skipped, not failed. `SecondBrain` is Mac-only and its absence on Windows is correct.

The "memory flow" line reports how long since `origin/main` on `global-memory` last advanced. Over 14 days it says so without failing: it cannot distinguish "quiet fortnight" from "the other machine's backup stopped pushing", and a check that cries wolf during the first gets ignored during the second.

## Two machines

`stack-check.ps1` tests `$env:OS -eq 'Windows_NT'` and swaps the machine-specific sections. Everything else (memsearch, flush pipeline, memory repos, cloud receipt, context budget, handoff) is shared.

| Section | Mac | Windows laptop |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs | launchd `com.keystone.*` agents | Task Scheduler: `Backup AI Sessions to Drive`, `DailyGmailDigest`, `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` (disabled tasks are skipped) |
| venv | `.venv/bin/python` | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` |
| memsearch backend | — | Docker Desktop `milvus-standalone` must be `(healthy)` |
| Backup state | `backup-state.json` (daily-backup) | `backup-ai-sessions-state.json` (daily). `Desktop\DEV` itself is a Drive for Desktop synced root; its weekly robocopy task was retired 2026-09-22 (XML in `~/.claude/scripts/retired/`) |
| SecondBrain | checked | skipped, it is Mac-only |

Windows issue codes:
- `task:<name>`: the last run exited non-zero. `3221225786` (0xC000013A, sleep/shutdown kill) only warns; the age check decides whether the job is really behind.
- `task-stale:<name>`, `task-never-run:<name>`, `task-missing:<name>`: the job is behind, has never run, or was deleted. Tasks live under `\Eric\`. Re-run with `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '<name>' | Start-ScheduledTask`; a bare `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName` fails with "cannot find the file specified".
- `task-dual-run:<name>`: a `KeystoneOS-*` task is enabled on Windows. The Mac owns those jobs and the data pulls; disable the Windows copy.
- `milvus-docker` / `milvus-down`: start Docker Desktop; memsearch hooks time out without it.
- `backup-missing:<tag>`, `backup-stale:<tag>`, `backup-error:<tag>`: read `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\AI_Sessions_Backup\<COMPUTERNAME>\_backup_log.txt`. The script silences robocopy, so re-run the robocopy line in the foreground to see which files failed (codes below 8 are success).

On the Windows laptop the weekly run is Task Scheduler task `\Eric\KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` (Mondays 10:30, pwsh 7). It is the one `KeystoneOS-*` task that stays enabled on Windows.

**Mac notes.** Jobs are **launchd user agents** in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. The script is PowerShell because `pwsh` runs it natively on both machines. PowerShell on macOS normalises `\` inside a path string to `/`, so the script's mixed separators resolve correctly — verified 2026-08-29. Do not "fix" them.

Useful launchd commands:
```bash
launchctl list | grep keystone                                    # loaded jobs + last exit code
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>                  # live schedule and state
launchctl bootout  gui/$(id -u)/com.keystone.<name>               # unload
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.<name>.plist   # reload
```
Edit a schedule with `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :StartCalendarInterval:Hour <n>" <plist>`, then bootout + bootstrap. **A plist edit alone does nothing until it is reloaded.**

## Weekly scheduled run

launchd agent `com.keystone.stackdoctor` (Mondays 10:30) runs `scripts/weekly-check.ps1`: the same read-only check, unattended. On failure it appends a one-line summary to `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` (surfaced at every session start per CLAUDE.md) and the full output is always in `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`. When a session surfaces such an entry, run this skill interactively to diagnose and fix, then clear the entry from `.errors.log`.

**Clearing `.errors.log`:** shell truncation (`: > file`) anywhere under `$HOME` is blocked by dcg rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`. Use `cp /dev/null <file>`. There is no `truncate` binary on this machine. Archive first — the lines are often live issues, not stale history:
```bash
cp ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log.archived-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cp /dev/null ~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log
```

## Known failure classes and fixes

These four classes have each bitten more than once (evidence: daily logs 2026-04 → 2026-07). Match the issue code to its fix:

### `task:*` / `task-stale:*` — launchd agent failed or didn't run
1. Read the `action:` line the script printed and run that exact command **manually in a foreground terminal** — launchd discards stdout unless the plist sets `StandardOutPath`; foreground shows the real error.
2. Known root causes: executable referenced without a full path (launchd agents get a minimal PATH — always use full paths like `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`, and set `EnvironmentVariables:PATH` in the plist); a plist edited but never `bootout`+`bootstrap`ed, so the old schedule is still live; the job firing at an hour the required volume is unmounted (see `backup-*`).
3. `launchctl list | grep keystone` shows each job's **last exit code** in column 2. A non-zero there with no output means the script's own log is the only evidence — check `~/.claude/scripts/logs/` and for a `*.log` beside the script.

### `venv-missing` / `venv-broken` — Python venv rot
The script checks `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/.venv/bin/python`.
macOS root causes: a Homebrew `python3` major-version bump orphans venvs built against the old interpreter; a `uv` reinstall or relocation breaks tools that hardcode `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv` (CLAUDE.md forbids relocating it for this reason).
Fix: recreate the venv (`uv sync` in the project, or `python3 -m venv .venv` + reinstall from its pyproject), then run the dependent agent once by hand to confirm.
*History (Windows box, retired 2026-08-14): Python Install Manager migrations deleted `C:\Python31x` twice, silently killing morning-briefing for 6 days. The lesson transfers — an interpreter move breaks every venv built on it — the paths do not.*

### `memsearch-path` / `memsearch-run` — memsearch CLI broken
memsearch is a **uv tool** on this machine: binary at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/memsearch`, environment at `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/`.
- Not on PATH or the binary errors → reinstall with `uv tool install --force memsearch`, not pip.
- Import failures inside the tool env (e.g. `onnxruntime`) are testable directly:
  `/Users/kristinarash/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/bin/python -c "import onnxruntime; print(onnxruntime.__version__)"`
- **After ANY reinstall/upgrade of memsearch the local flush patch is stripped.** Re-apply it (notes in `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/`), then confirm `.errors.log` stays empty for a session.
- `INDEX full set: Indexed 0 chunks` in the nightly log is **usually not an indexer fault** — it means nothing new arrived. Check `flush-stale` first; a dead flush pipeline starves the indexer and looks identical (confirmed 2026-08-29).

### `recall-coverage` / `recall-regress` — memory search can't find what it should
- `recall-coverage`: a root in `KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` doesn't exist on this machine, so it is never indexed (the hooks skip missing roots; `memsearch-sync.js` lists them at the top of `.memsearch-index.log`). Paths take `{HOME}`, `{DEV}` and `{VAULT}`; a machine-specific location needs a token, not a hardcoded path. The other machine's Tier A slug is the one expected miss.
- `recall-regress`: hit@5 fell by 2+ between this machine's last two runs of a backend in `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/ledger.md`.
- **The eval:** `python ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/recall-eval.py --label "<model or change>"` (add `--backends fts5,rg` when Docker is down or RAM is short). Known-answer cases live in `questions.jsonl`. Rerun after a model change, a memsearch/context-mode upgrade, or any edit to the index paths. **Scheduled (Windows):** Task Scheduler `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` (Sundays 02:00) runs reindex → eval (all four backends, label `weekly`) → `audits/recall-eval/after-run.ps1`, which commits+pushes the results, writes `LATEST.md`, and only on a problem appends to `.errors.log`. Spec and decision rule: `~/.claude/audits/2026-09-30-memory-infra-audit.md` §6.

### `errors-log` / `flush-stale` / `flush-error` / `flush-missing` — memory pipeline
- `.errors.log` non-empty → read the entries **before clearing**; they are frequently live unresolved issues rather than stale history. Common causes: the stripped memsearch flush patch (above), or an Agent SDK timeout ("Control request timeout: initialize" — transient, but recurring daily means the hook environment is broken).
- `last-flush.json` stale >48h → check `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.log` tail for the real error. `last-flush.json` is written by `flush.py` **only on success**, so a stale timestamp means flushes are dying, not that the hook never fired.
- **Stranded context files are the tell.** `session-end.py` writes `scripts/session-flush-<session>-<stamp>.md` then spawns `flush.py`, which **deletes that file on success**. So every leftover `session-flush-*.md` in `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/` is a flush that died, and its date maps to a missing `daily/<date>.md`.
  Recover one by re-running it by hand (~1 min, writes into the daily log):
  ```bash
  /Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/uv run --directory ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler \
    python ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/scripts/flush.py <context-file> <session-id>
  ```
  Success looks like `Result: FLUSH_OK` + `Flush complete` in `flush.log`.
- No `SessionEnd fired` lines in `flush.log` for days, yet the hook works when run by hand → sessions are being closed rather than exited cleanly. Self-verifying: end one session normally and re-check the tail.
- FLUSH_ERROR in dailies → same investigation; `flush.log` is ground truth.

### `backup-*` — daily backup rot
launchd agent `com.keystone.dailybackup` (**21:00 daily** since 2026-09-24; 09:00 from 2026-08-29) runs `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`: auto-commits+pushes the memory repos (SecondBrain, dotclaude, claude-skills, claude-global-memory), **rsync**-snapshots `~/.claude/projects`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini` and non-repo DEV folders to Google Drive at `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/…`, captures the same set to the **CRASHBOX SSD** at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/` when it is mounted, runs an uncapped full memsearch reindex, and resets the hook's timeout-streak counter. Restore procedure: `~/.claude/RESTORE.md`.

**The SSD layer's signature failure — a clean exit code is not evidence.** If CRASHBOX is unmounted the run logs `TARGET SSD … NOT MOUNTED … SKIPPED` and still ends `OK (0 errors)`. The schedule moved 00:30 → 09:00 on 2026-08-29 precisely because the drive was never attached at 00:30. **Verify an SSD capture only by a fresh receipt** at `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup/_receipts/run-*.txt`. Never by directory mtimes (`rsync -a` preserves source mtimes, and a parent dir's mtime moves only when an entry is added or removed — top-level SSD dirs legitimately show weeks-old dates after a perfect capture) and never by `du`. `-DryRun` runs `rsync -n` and proves nothing about writes.
- `backup-missing` / `backup-stale` → job didn't run; re-run foreground (~6 min): `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`. There is no SSD-only switch, and one should not be added.
- `backup-error` → read `~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`; a `repo-diverged:*` entry means a memory repo has both remote and local changes — reconcile manually (the script refuses to merge from automation).
- `backup-repo-drift:*` → pushes failing (>3 unpushed commits); usually gh/git auth rot — run `gh auth status`.
- `backup-cloud-*` → the Drive-API heartbeat (gws CLI queries RESTORE.md's cloud modifiedTime). `-check` = gws auth rot; re-auth needs explicit full scope URLs: `gws auth login --scopes "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly"` (the `-s drive` shorthand silently grants NO scopes, v0.22.5 bug). After re-auth delete `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json` or it serves the stale token. The login is interactive — Eric must run it himself via `!` while at the machine, then open the printed URL directly; terminal copy/paste truncates it at line-wrap. `-stale`/`-missing` = files reach the local CloudStorage cache but Google Drive for Desktop isn't syncing — check that Google Drive is running and signed in.
- Drive is a **FUSE CloudStorage mount**: it rounds mtimes it did not write, so `rsync -a` re-sends identical files forever. Use `--modify-window=5`; never `--size-only`.

## Not covered by the script (check manually if symptoms point there)

- **MCP/plugin auth rot** (9 manual fix-it sessions on record): run `claude doctor` / `claude mcp list` and re-auth any claude.ai connectors showing failures (Supabase, Vercel, Google Calendar have all rotted before).
- **Catapult OpenField token expiry**: see the auth section of `pp-catapult-openfield-connect`.

## Gotchas

- **`flush.py` always writes into *today's* daily log.** Recovering a weeks-old stranded `session-flush-*.md` files old facts under today's date, and the compiler then treats them as current. Recover only recent ones. Move old ones to `scripts/_stranded-archive/` so a file left in `scripts/` still means a flush that died recently (3 files from June archived 2026-09-22).
- **Drive's `name contains` is token matching, not substring.** The cloud check's `run-2` query also returned `jev_run2.jsonl`, so results are filtered to `run-*.txt` on the client.
- **Desktop Commander MCP times out at session start on Windows.** It starts through `npx -y …@latest`, which checks the npm registry every time: 23s alone, 30–46s alongside the other servers, against a 30s default. `MCP_TIMEOUT=90000` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `env` fixes it (set 2026-09-22). If it times out again, raise the timeout; don't edit the synced plugin's `plugin.json`, which is re-synced on the next launch.
- **Stale `.git/worktrees/<name>` dirs that `git worktree prune` can't delete ("Permission denied") are not locked.** Their empty `logs`/`refs` subfolders are read-only; `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force <dir>` clears them (2026-09-22, with Drive quit and prune still failing).
- **`flush.log` "SKIP: transcript missing" is not a fault.** It comes from sessions that were opened and closed before any message was sent, so there is nothing to flush.

## Rules

- Read-only by default: the script never mutates state. Fixes are applied by you, deliberately, after reporting findings.
- Don't assume the obvious culprit — a signal that pattern-matches a known failure may have a different cause (lesson: 6/25 Milvus/ETIMEDOUT misdiagnosis). Confirm with the foreground re-run before fixing.
- When a fix is applied, re-run the script to verify the issue code clears, and note the incident in memory if it's a new failure class.

<system-reminder>
The following skills were invoked EARLIER in this session (before the conversation was compacted), not on the current turn. They are shown here for context only so you remain aware of their guidelines.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT re-execute these skills or perform their one-time setup actions (e.g., scheduling, creating files) again. Any request or argument text embedded in the skill bodies below — for example under a "## User Request" or "## Input" heading — was captured when that skill was first invoked. It is NOT the user's current message and NOT a new request: do not act on it as if it were live. Only continue to apply ongoing behavioral guidelines from these skills where still relevant.

### Skill: closeout
Path: userSettings:closeout

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

Never by directory mtimes (`rsync -a` preserves source mtimes, and a parent dir's mtime moves only when an entry is added or removed — top-level SSD dirs legitimately show weeks-old dates after a perfect capture) and never by `du`. `-DryRun` runs `rsync -n` and proves nothing about writes.
- `backup-missing` / `backup-stale` → job didn't run; re-run foreground (~6 min): `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -File ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`. There is no SSD-only switch, and one should not be added.
- `backup-error` → read `~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`; a `repo-diverged:*` entry means a memory repo has both remote and local changes — reconcile manually (the script refuses to merge from automation).
- `backup-repo-drift:*` → pushes failing (>3 unpushed commits); usually gh/git auth rot — run `gh auth status`.
- `backup-cloud-*` → the Drive-API heartbeat (gws CLI queries RESTORE.md's cloud modifiedTime). `-check` = gws auth rot; re-auth needs explicit full scope URLs: `gws auth login --scopes "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly"` (the `-s drive` shorthand silently grants NO scopes, v0.22.5 bug). After re-auth delete `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json` or it serves the stale token. The login is interactive — Eric must run it himself via `!` while at the machine, then open the printed URL directly; terminal copy/paste truncates it at line-wrap. `-stale`/`-missing` = files reach the local CloudStorage cache but Google Drive for Desktop isn't syncing — check that Google Drive is running and signed in.
- Drive is a **FUSE CloudStorage mount**: it rounds mtimes it did not write, so `rsync -a` re-sends identical files forever. Use `--modify-window=5`; never `--size-only`.

## Not covered by the script (check manually if symptoms point there)

- **MCP/plugin auth rot** (9 manual fix-it sessions on record): run `claude doctor` / `claude mcp list` and re-auth any claude.ai connectors showing failures (Supabase, Vercel, Google Calendar have all rotted before).
- **Catapult OpenField token expiry**: see the auth section of `pp-catapult-openfield-connect`.

## Gotchas

- **`flush.py` always writes into *today's* daily log.** Recovering a weeks-old stranded `session-flush-*.md` files old facts under today's date, and the compiler then treats them as current. Recover only recent ones. Move old ones to `scripts/_stranded-archive/` so a file left in `scripts/` still means a flush that died recently (3 files from June archived 2026-09-22).
- **Drive's `name contains` is token matching, not substring.** The cloud check's `run-2` query also returned `jev_run2.jsonl`, so results are filtered to `run-*.txt` on the client.
- **Desktop Commander MCP times out at session start on Windows.** It starts through `npx -y …@latest`, which checks the npm registry every time: 23s alone, 30–46s alongside the other servers, against a 30s default. `MCP_TIMEOUT=90000` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `env` fixes it (set 2026-09-22). If it times out again, raise the timeout; don't edit the synced plugin's `plugin.json`, which is re-synced on the next launch.
- **Stale `.git/worktrees/<name>` dirs that `git worktree prune` can't delete ("Permission denied") are not locked.** Their empty `logs`/`refs` subfolders are read-only; `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force <dir>` clears them (2026-09-22, with Drive quit and prune still failing).
- **`flush.log` "SKIP: transcript missing" is not a fault.** It comes from sessions that were opened and closed before any message was sent, so there is nothing to flush.

## Rules

- Read-only by default: the script never mutates state. Fixes are applied by you, deliberately, after reporting findings.
- Don't assume the obvious culprit — a signal that pattern-matches a known failure may have a different cause (lesson: 6/25 Milvus/ETIMEDOUT misdiagnosis). Confirm with the foreground re-run before fixing.
- When a fix is applied, re-run the script to verify the issue code clears, and note the incident in memory if it's a new failure class.

</system-reminder>

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

objective.description: Optional broader goal for this search, if known. Avoid sensitive information.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. A search with sources: ["web"] omits semantic provider discovery; domainTools: true can still return website-matched tools. Web-only results use domainTools: false. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. # Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

The default daemon can keep many tabs and visit many sites; browser-use has
no per-site, screenshot, or result-count limit that requires a new daemon.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.

  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
